Hi Sergio,

Thanks for sending the draft. Attached are our suggested redlines (see Redlines_Ridgewell_v1.docx). A few commercial items we need clarity on before we can proceed to PO: 

- Invoice recipient / entity: Our AP team requires either (A) consolidated invoice from Redwood US or (B) split invoicing per Ridgewell legal entity (US / EU). Can you confirm if Redwood can support per-entity invoices?
- Taxes / VAT: For EU usage, do you expect Ridgewell to pay VAT, or can Redwood zero-rate under reverse-charge? If you need tax residency docs from us, confirm what format we should send.
- Minimum commit proration: The redlines propose a quarterly true-up rather than monthly. We need to understand how proration works mid-term if we scale above commit.
- Net terms: We usually run Net45 but can look at Net30 for larger vendors. Your contract shows Net30 — is Net45 possible?
- PO + invoicing cadence: We plan to issue a PO within two weeks contingent on these clarifications. Also, please confirm whether Redwood requires a PO number on the invoice for payment.

Appreciate a short response with options by end of week so our procurement and finance teams can align.

Best,

Ari Thomson
Head of Procurement, Ridgewell Analytics
ari.thomson@ridgewell.ai

Forwarding Ridgewell's redlines — key asks below. TL;DR: They want flexibility on invoice entity and net terms; tax evidence and PO timing will be gating.

On Wed, 4 Aug 2027 at 09:12, Ari Thomson <ari.thomson@ridgewell.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sergio,
> 
> Thanks for sending the draft...

Notes / suggested approach: 
- Invoicing: Offer both options but prefer consolidated invoice for simplicity. If we accept split invoicing, require documented billing entity list + AP emails and expect some operational lead time (~2 billing cycles) to set up.
- Taxes: Ask Ridgewell to provide a tax residency / VAT registration certificate for EU reverse-charge. If they cannot provide, Redwood will invoice VAT where applicable.
- Minimum commit proration: Propose quarterly true-up with a mid-quarter prorate on committed units; if usage exceeds commit, pay overage at list price, with a cap in first 90 days to protect them.
- Net terms: Sales target Net30, Finance prefers Net45 for new customers. Offer Net45 for first 12 months; Net30 thereafter conditioned on credit reference.
- PO requirement: We can accept PO on invoices but do not require PO string for acceptance — payment will be processed only if PO is present. Recommend asking them to route invoices to ap@ridgewell.ai and cc contracts.

Action items: 
1) Ben — confirm if Sales discount up to 10% can be approved to close this quarter (they're asking for a 7% on the first-year commit).
2) Monica — can Finance sign off on Net45 for year one? Also confirm VAT handling and whether Redwood will register in EU or rely on reverse-charge.
3) Laura — any MSA redlines in the attached doc that we should push back on aggressively (indemnity, data handling language)?

I'll draft a reply to Ridgewell after we align.

--
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the summary, Sergio. Quick answers from finance/legal viewpoint: 

- Discount: I can approve up to 8% on the first-year commit if we get a 12-month minimum and a signed SOW + PO within 30 days. Anything beyond 8% needs CRO/RevOps sign-off.
- Net terms: Finance will accept Net45 for the first 12 months as a concession to close, subject to a credit check. We'll move to Net30 after the initial period.
- VAT registration: Redwood will not register in EU for this account. We will invoice with VAT where required unless Ridgewell provides EU VAT registration + tax residency certificate to enable reverse-charge. Monica, confirm if we need any additional evidence.
- Split invoicing: Ops can support split invoicing per legal entity but it requires a short ops setup (2 billing cycles) and an explicit list of billing entities and AP contacts. There will be an operational fee for multi-entity invoicing — propose a one-time $750 setup fee (to cover accounting runbooks).
- Proration: Agree on quarterly true-up. For mid-quarter scale-ups, apply pro-rata charge on the next invoice; provide a cap at 150% of monthly committed units for the first full quarter to avoid bill shocks.

I'll attach an updated Order Form (OrderForm_Ridgewell_v3.pdf) that reflects the above options and a tracked-changes summary for Laura. Sergio, if you can share which option Ridgewell prefers (consolidated vs split) I'll prepare the final redlines and a DocuSign packet.

Regards,

Ben Carter

ben_carter@redwood.com

Sergio / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. Ridgewell's procurement discussed internally and here's what we can commit to: 

- Invoicing: We will accept split invoicing by legal entity. Please invoice the EU entity for EU usage and the US entity for US usage. We'll provide the list of legal entities and AP contacts by Friday (AP emails will be ap@ridgewell.ai for US and eu-ap@ridgewell.ai for EU).
- Taxes: We'll provide our EU VAT registration and a signed tax residency certificate (TaxResidency_Ridgewell.pdf) by COB Friday so you can apply reverse-charge where applicable.
- Minimum commit / proration: We accept the quarterly true-up with the proposed pro-rata on the next invoice. The 150% cap for the first quarter is acceptable.
- Net terms: Net45 for the first 12 months is fine. We will provide a PO (PO# R-8492) once we receive the final Order Form. Please include the PO number on all invoices.
- Setup fee: We're okay with the one-time $750 multi-entity billing setup charge. Please include this as a separate line item on the first invoice.

Next steps: Please send the final Order Form with tracked changes and a DocuSign link. We'll route the PO and tax docs as requested.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this signed.

Regards,
